DATE
2026-09-17

ADDED
• UIbasic v1.0 integration through an ARGOS adapter.
• TINY, COMPACT, FULL, and AUTO status modes.
• Truthful workflow-state and measurable-progress presentation rules.
• Persistent checkpoint/recovery presentation.
• State-aware next-step engine with RECOMMENDED / OPTIONAL / REQUIRES INPUT / AUTO-CONTINUE.
• ARGOS/UIbasic shared status mapping.
• UIbasic status templates.
• QA checks for UI state, progress, persistence, recovery, artifacts, and regression.

CHANGED
• UI AUTO is now the default ARGOS presentation behavior.
• Autonomous processing can use TINY status without interrupting continuation.
• Milestones, blockers, QA gates, failures, and completion use FULL presentation.
• Existing ARGOS persistent state remains authoritative; UIbasic cannot create duplicate state/progress systems.

COMPATIBILITY NOTES
• v1.8 is backward-compatible with v1.3 research architecture.
• UIbasic is an external protocol integrated by adapter.
• Existing validated ARGOS work remains authoritative.

• Existing validated ARGOS work remains authoritative unless specifically superseded.

ARGOS — Academic Research Governance, Opposition & Synthesis — v1.8

FUNCTIONAL MEANING
ARGOS expands to Academic Research Governance, Opposition & Synthesis.

CONCEPTUAL MEANING
Argos evokes the watchful guardian of Greek mythology: observant, difficult to deceive, and able to keep many things under scrutiny at once. The name fits a research framework that watches evidence from multiple expert perspectives, verifies sources, challenges assumptions, searches for contradictions, and keeps the full research problem in view before synthesizing conclusions.

PROJECT PURPOSE
ARGOS is the CASPER-derived academic, scientific, technical, R&D, policy, standards, and official-research framework. It accepts a question and/or source material, assembles an appropriate 10–15-expert panel, researches and validates evidence, opposes premature conclusions through adversarial review, and produces streamlined professional publications.
